blurb: Lamb-like terrier from a Northumberland mining town, fast on land and in water
description: The Bedlington Terrier is a small English terrier from Northumberland with a lamb-like look, a linty non-shedding coat and a mild but plucky character.
answer: The Bedlington Terrier is a small terrier named after the mining town of Bedlington in Northumberland, England, originally bred to hunt vermin. It stands about 41 cm tall, weighs roughly 8 to 10 kg, and is known for its lamb-like appearance and a temperament described as both gentle and tenacious.

body: Once called the Rothbury or Rodbury Terrier, and earlier used by Romani people and poachers for hunting, the breed was a favourite of northern miners. Some pedigrees trace back to 1782, and the name Bedlington Terrier was first applied in 1825 to a dog called Young Piper. The dogs hunted otters, badgers and rabbits and were raced until the Whippet became more popular.

The first show class for the breed was held at Bedlington in 1870, and the Bedlington Terrier Club was founded in 1875. The breed is closely related to the Dandie Dinmont Terrier and probably the Whippet and Otterhound. In 1948 a Bedlington won Best in Show at Westminster.

The Bedlington is often said to resemble a lamb. It has a rounded head with no stop, small almond-shaped eyes, an arched back and a light, springy gait. Colours are blue, liver or sandy, each possibly with tan points, and puppies born dark lighten with age. The coat mixes hard and soft hairs, forms a topknot on the head and is described as non-shedding with minimal odour.

The AKC and ASPCA describe the breed as mild and gentle and good with children, and others call it loyal, playful and a quiet house dog. It is also described as plucky, tenacious with vermin, sometimes high-strung or headstrong, and inclined to bolt. The New Zealand Kennel Club cautions against keeping it with dominant dogs, though it is otherwise said to get on with other dogs.

The Bedlington is fast with high endurance and a strong swimmer. Its coat needs regular, at least weekly grooming to remove dead hair; a show clip is difficult to maintain, so most pets are kept in a simpler pet groom.

One 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.7 years. The breed has a high incidence of copper toxicosis, an inherited liver disorder, and DNA testing of breeding stock has significantly reduced it. Other conditions reported in the breed include heart murmur, kidney problems and eye problems such as epiphora, retinal dysplasia and cataracts.

faq.a: The coat is described as non-shedding with minimal odour, but it needs at least weekly grooming to remove dead hair.

faq.q: How long do Bedlington Terriers live?
faq.a: One 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.7 years, above the average for purebred dogs.

faq.q: Why does a Bedlington Terrier look like a lamb?
faq.a: Its rounded head, topknot and soft, linty coat in blue, liver or sandy shades give it a lamb-like look, which led to the old nickname Rothbury's Lambs.
